they commanded the Franks who were in their military service
to go up to the monastery and cut Mouzalon in pieces with swords,
wherever he might be.
And when they went up,
they found him in the church while praying,
and there they cut him limb from limb.
And the nobles also went up,
and cried out in a loud voice:
“Long live the king of the Greeks, Michael Palaiologos!
Long live the autokrator of the Romans, Michael Palaiologos!”
And from there they all went to Nicaea,
and they seized the boy Kaloyan,
and sent and imprisoned him in one of the fortresses.
And also Arsenios the patriarch,
who rebuked them for his murder,
they sent into exile to a certain monastery on one of the islands of the Pontic Sea.
And a little while after that Michael became king,
he resolved in his mind to march against Constantinople,
because he heard that there was a small force in it with Baldwin, the Frankish king, its master.
And during this march of his, he sent and fetched Nikephoros, the metropolitan of Ephesus,
and made him patriarch in the city of Gallipoli in place of Arsenios, who had been rejected.
And he set out from there and went and encamped against Constantinople,
but was unable to capture it,
because the citizens, along with the soldiers, stoutly stood upon the walls and fought fiercely.
And when Michael saw that he was not succeeding,
he abandoned it and returned.
And after a short time,
the Frankish merchants who are called Venetians in the city of Acre and those who are called Genoese engaged in conflict with one another,
and the Pisans also joined the Venetians.
And when the Venetians who were in all the lands heard,
they ran without delay to the aid of their comrades,
and Constantinople was also emptied of them.
And that Michael again devised another stratagem,
and he said to a certain commander of a fortress of his,
that he should show rebellion and send to Baldwin that he should send a force,
so that he might surrender that fortress to him.
And that commander of the fortress did so,
and he enticed and deceived Baldwin.
